To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a performance model for OpenCL kernels and apply it to analyze the resource requirement of convolutional neural network kernels and available resources of modern FPGAs; we identify that the key bottleneck is on-chip memory bandwidth and propose a new kernel structure to effectively address the bandwidth limitation; and we design an FPGA-based accelerator for convolutional neural networks based on the proposed techniques.

the key performance limitation of OpenCL FPGA for CNN is the on-chip memory bandwidth and that a new kernel design is proposed to address such limitation and to provide the optimal balance between computation and memory access.
the on-chip memory bandwidth becomes the performance bottleneck for CNN classifiers on modern FPGas and that a new kernel design is needed to address the bandwidth limitation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance optimization of OpenCL FPGA for both compute-intensive workloads such CNN and general purpose kernels.
the design of high-performance OpenCL kernels for FPGAs.
optimizing the performance of OpenCL FPGA for CNN applications, which is a very challenging and important topic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed techniques are general and applicable to a wide range of CNN models.
we have proposed a novel design for FPGA-based CNN acceleration, and the proposed design achieves the best power and area efficiency compared to the state-of-the-art FPGA-based CNN accelerator.
we propose an analytical performance modeling and optimization methodology to design OpenCL kernels for FPGAs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a new kernel design and a new memory access pattern to efficiently utilize the FPGA hardware resources.
our work is able to achieve the state-of-the-art performance for CNN accelerator design on FPGA.
our design is 2.5x more power efficient and 2.1x more performance efficient than the state of art.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the onchip memory bottleneck is the main performance bottleneck for CNN kernels.
the performance bottleneck in modern FPGAs is the onchip bandwidth.
the performance of CNN accelerator can be significantly improved by carefully balancing computation, memory, and communication resources in the FPGA.
